title: Average latency with abandoned requests
prompt: Some callers give up before the API answers; those requests have no `latency_ms`. Write `solve(api_requests)` with pair RDD functions so it returns, per `endpoint`, how many requests it had, how many have a latency, and their average latency.
rules: One row per `endpoint`; requests with no endpoint are grouped together under a missing endpoint.
`requests` counts every request; `timed` counts those with a `latency_ms`.
`avg_latency_ms` is the average of the latencies that are there, not rounded. A missing latency is left out, never treated as 0; an endpoint with no latency at all has a missing average.
hints: Carry three numbers per request: `(1, 1 if it has a latency else 0, latency or 0)`.
`reduceByKey` adds the three parts; the average is the total divided by `timed`, computed once at the end.
Dividing by a `timed` of 0 raises. Return `None` for those endpoints, and use `/`, not `//`.
explanation: Map each request to `(endpoint, (1, has_latency, latency or 0))`, add the three parts with `reduceByKey`, then divide the total by `timed` at the end, giving `None` when `timed` is 0. Counting a missing latency as 0 drags the average down, dropping the untimed requests up front loses them from `requests` (and loses an endpoint whose callers all gave up), and `//` cuts the fraction off, so 42.75 becomes 42.
